title: review (other model): C-O2a host-portable auth and secrets (T-0079)
spec: Review the diff of T-0079 (branch task/T-0079, worktree wt/T-0079) against its acceptance. Executed by claude:sonnet as the Codex fallback, so this review is on opus. Check especially: the token value never reaches a log line, the bus, or the run log (grep the diff for print/log/json.dumps of env values); CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is only set when the account has oauth_token_env AND the variable is set, and is absent otherwise; the env: secret form skips a missing variable with a note naming the variable, not the value; the command form is byte-for-byte the old behaviour; pool.toml still parses with tomllib and its values are unchanged; existing tests untouched. Verdict approve or request_changes with path:line findings.
acceptance: Each acceptance criterion of T-0079 marked met or not met with evidence

comments.issue: Accounts WITHOUT oauth_token_env still inherit an ambient CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN from the daemon's environment, because env = {**os.environ, ...}. `claude setup-token` prints a token under that exact canonical name, so the obvious headless setup (export CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN for account A, oauth_token_env=TOK_B for B) silently runs every unconfigured account under A's identity, overriding the CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR binding that the module docstring promises. That breaks per-account rate-limit accounting and the other-account guarantees (review on a different account, challenge on account B). Fix is one line: else branch doing env.pop('CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN', None). The new test's setUp scrubs the ambient var precisely because this pass-through exists, so it is not covered. Not a regression of prior behaviour, hence not blocking.

`if val:` treats an env var that is set but empty as missing, and the stderr note then claims "env var X is not set", which is wrong for the empty case. An operator debugging a truncated systemd EnvironmentFile gets a misleading message. Use `val is not None` or word the note as "not set or empty".

setUp replaces Popen on the shared subprocess module (spawn.subprocess IS subprocess), so every subprocess.run in the process is also rerouted through FakePopen for the duration. It only passes today because [secrets.execute] is absent from pool.toml and the task dict presets worktree; adding a [secrets.execute] entry later makes secrets_for_role call subprocess.run -> FakePopen.communicate(input=...) -> TypeError, with no hint that the cause is the patch. Patch spawn's own reference or accept **kwargs in FakePopen.communicate.

The new option is only documented in README: pool.toml's [[claude_accounts]] tables carry no commented `oauth_token_env = "..."` example, unlike the env: form which did get an inline comment. A reader configuring a headless host from the config file alone will not discover the key. Spec item (4) only mandated the secrets comment, so this is a doc gap, not a missed criterion.
